Nothing is saved yet. 8c.3b Step 3: the id follows the title; Save rule. Then add a rule with id layer-name, and one with pattern (. The rule appears under Company. The others are refused (already used, not a valid regular expression). 8c.4 Export → Markdown. In a shell: bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --practices --profile kas-wrynose; echo "exit $?", then with --fail-on never. The report downloads; the CLI prints the same review and exits 2 with errors, 0 with --fail-on never. 8c.5 Delete the rule and

title: Stage 9 — Projects, setup and notifications (no builds)
text: # Do You should see 9.1 9, w (projects). Recent projects; the active one marked active. 9.2 o, Enter on the project folder (the Bitloom checkout). Then o again with ~/bitloom-kas-wrynose. The checkout: kas proposals for kas-minimal.yml and kas-wrynose.yml with evidence. The work directory: only a host proposal, marked as the kas work directory of kas-wrynose with a warning to switch with P instead. Esc without saving. Web: 8 → Set up a project shows the same. 9.3 n (new project). Release, MACHINE, image and runtime fields with a live preview; Esc without creating. 9.4 9, o, ^T. A test notification arrives.

title: Stage 10 — Web extras (no builds)
text: # Do You should see 10.1 The bell button, allow notifications; switch to another tab and run a short build from the TUI. A browser notification when it ends. 10.2 Narrow the window to phone width (or the browser's device mode). One column; the navigation becomes a scrolling bar; nothing scrolls sideways. 10.3 Switch the operating system to light theme. The dashboard follows it.

title: Stage 11 — Command line and CI (≈30 seconds)
text: bitloom --state .validation --service-stop # after closing the TUI and the web server bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --state .validation --ci build:busybox --profile kas-wrynose \ --junit /tmp/results.xml --summary /tmp/summary.json # ≈10 s, PASS line, JUnit and JSON written bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --state .validation --vulns --min-cvss 9 --fail-on-unpatched; echo "exit $?" # exit 2 bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --state .validation --vulns --format md -o /tmp/vulns.md bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --cra; bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --doctor --network --ci runs its own serial queue on the state directory, so first close the web server (Ctrl+C) and the TUI (Ctrl+Q) and stop the idle service: bitloom --state .validation --service-stop. The other commands only read and work at any time.

title: Stage 12 — Finish
text: If they are still open, close the web server with Ctrl+C and the TUI with Ctrl+Q, then bitloom --state .validation --service-stop. Builds already done stay in the work directories; nothing else needs cleaning except the Studio files of step 7.5.

title: B01 — Fresh checkout and demo
text: Requires Linux/WSL2, Bash, Python 3.10+ with venv support and internet access. ./setup-demo.sh --dev --no-launch source .venv/bin/activate bitloom --help python -m bitloom --list-actions COLORTERM=truecolor bitloom --demo Expected: .venv is created/reused, the executable and module work, and the demo opens. The demo provides sample files; it does not provide BitBake or fabricate successful Yocto builds. Exit with Ctrl+Q; Esc closes a dialog first. Repeat setup: existing sample files are retained. Press P: the switcher lists demo, demo-scarthgap and demo-wrynose. Select each: the top bar shows release unknown, scarthgap 5.0 LTS and wrynose 6.0 LTS respectively. The workspaces live in .bitloom/demo, .bitloom/demo-scarthgap and .bitloom/demo-wrynose; every SBOM/CVE sample names itself a demo sample.

title: B02 — Wheel and source archive
text: python -m pip install build wheel python -m build --no-isolation Expected: dist/bitloom-<project-version>.tar.gz and dist/bitloom-<project-version>-py3-none-any.whl. Install the wheel into a separate venv and run its bitloom --help from outside the checkout. Extract the source archive and verify LICENSE, setup-demo.sh, this testbook, examples, tools and docs are present.

title: B03 — Debian release package
text: On a system providing dpkg-deb: python tools/build_release.py 0.9.0 --output dist/manual-release-0.9.0 (cd dist/manual-release-0.9.0 && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS) dpkg-deb --info dist/manual-release-0.9.0/bitloom_0.9.0_all.deb Use a new output directory if repeating. Expected: source, wheel, .deb and checksums use version 0.9.0; the checkout's version stays unchanged. Install the .deb in a disposable Debian/Ubuntu machine/container with Python 3.10+ using sudo apt install ./bitloom_0.9.0_all.deb. Run /usr/bin/bitloom --help from /tmp; verify dependencies under /opt/bitloom/lib and MIT license under /usr/share/doc/bitloom/copyright. Remove with sudo apt remove bitloom. Publishing a GitHub release is a separate operator action and is not required by this testbook.

title: 2. Launch with kas-container
text: Docker or Podman must already work. Keep Yocto work files on a Linux filesystem. Bitloom itself can reside in the current checkout. The pinned kas image provides the Yocto toolchain dependencies. source .venv/bin/activate curl -fL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/siemens/kas/4.8.1/kas-container \ -o .venv/bin/kas-container chmod +x .venv/bin/kas-container docker info

title: K01 — Reuse this checkout's verified build
text: If .validation/result.json exists: python tools/prepare_validation.py COLORTERM=truecolor bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --state .validation F4 provides both a JSON editor and Clone. Clone chooses a unique name and distinct absolute build directory; it preserves the original profile. Developer also provides Clone through F10. Expected: kas-integration profile, kas-container runtime, qemux86-64/poky. The helper preserves history and takes KAS_WORK_DIR from the recorded result. With Docker Snap the daemon's /tmp can differ from host /tmp. Use runtime file operations with /work/build; an empty host directory does not prove the container build is missing. Use this path for read-only inspection or routine rebuilds. A saved result does not prove the temporary work mount still exists: use F10 Runtime browser to check /work/build. If it was removed, use K02 or K04 for a fresh workspace. Use an isolated profile for tests that change configuration, devtool state or caches.

title: K02 — Prepare an isolated manual-test profile
text: Run from the checkout with the venv activated. This writes a new state/configuration directory, without touching .validation or the integration YAML: python - <<'PY' from pathlib import Path from bitloom.models import Profile, Settings root = Path.cwd().resolve() settings = Settings(root / '.manual-testbook/profiles.json') if settings.path.exists(): raise SystemExit('Manual profiles already exist; reuse them or choose a new state directory.') settings.profiles = [Profile( name='manual-kas', root=str(root), mode='kas-container', kas_file='tests/integration/kas-minimal.yml', machine='qemux86-64', distro='poky', targets=['core-image-minimal'], environment={ 'KAS_CONTAINER_ENGINE': 'docker', 'KAS_WORK_DIR': '/tmp/bitloom-manual-work', 'KAS_CONTAINER_IMAGE': 'ghcr.io/siemens/kas/kas@sha256:fef6f850106a6823e65e133ed8157a847431dea4aa2de3a636c11f65e9977476', })] settings.active = 'manual-kas' settings.save() PY COLORTERM=truecolor bitloom \ --config .manual-testbook/profiles.json --state .manual-testbook Before the first checkout, open F10 → Runtime capabilities → Prepare new kas workspace → Run. This prepares the dedicated empty container work directory if its daemon-side ownership differs. For Podman change KAS_CONTAINER_ENGINE and use podman info. This dedicated workspace may require a cold build. Existing edits to the base integration YAML are included; record its Git diff before testing.

title: K03 — Checkout and validate configuration
text: F2 → Checkout kas repositories; then Dump resolved kas configuration. Expected: checked-out pinned Poky revision and the merged machine/distro/target. In Analysis run Build preflight on /work/build; missing build configuration before the first build is a prerequisite finding, not a fake PASS. Build busybox, then core-image-minimal to populate pkgdata, artifacts and reports needed below. Run Generate kas lock file and inspect its actual output; kas release support determines the result.

title: K04 — Automated real Developer fixture setup
text: For a new isolated real workspace, after installing the official wrapper above: python tools/validate_developer.py --build COLORTERM=truecolor bitloom --config .developer-validation/profiles.json \ --state .developer-validation/manual Docker is the default. --engine podman selects Podman; --work /absolute/new/workspace selects another work mount. --image additionally builds core-image-minimal with the generated package. The helper probes actual metadata, creates a uniquely named local layer/YAML, builds a small data-only CLOSED recipe, prepares sources, verifies fetch and recipe build with BB_NO_NETWORK, introduces/restores a controlled do_install failure, and saves result.json plus actual logs. The fixture deliberately keeps the initial build smaller than the complete image; TUI templates are separate MIT-licensed source examples. Repeating retains older evidence and creates new unique overlays/layers. Expected: every successful operation has a log/exit result. Missing image/buildhistory artifacts before --image remain unavailable. In F10 set recipe to bitloom-validation-hello, inspect Recipe context and SUMMARY, browse /work, then create your own fixture for chapter 13. Use a new state directory for manual work so automated history remains separate. This can take several minutes and download/build native dependencies on a cold workspace.

title: 3. UI and profile acceptance
text: Case Steps Expected result U01 F8/F9 through all sections, including Analysis and Help; Ctrl+L; Ctrl+P Navigation works; log focus and command palette open. Alt+number is optional terminal-dependent behavior, not the primary shortcut. U02 F2 filter by fetch, layer and devtool; choose an action; leave a required field blank Matching actions appear; missing input is rejected before submission; preview matches argv. U03 F4 duplicate manual-kas, rename it, edit targets/environment and select it Named profile persists after restart; the selected profile drives new jobs. Invalid mode/duplicate names/environment types are rejected. U04 Resize to 160×50, 120×36, 90×28, 80×24, 60×20, 140×20, then back Logs remain usable, secondary panels disappear, and panels return when space is available. F2/F4/F7 dialogs fit at 60×20. U05 F7 preview all fourteen themes, Cancel; repeat, Save Soft Slate or Linen and restart with the same state Cancel restores the old palette; Save persists. Focus a report pane: the border changes, its background stays stable. U06 Inspect CPU/RAM and filesystem cards Values update and are labelled host measurements, including with container profiles. Machine/distro header reflects explicit/literal settings; evaluated environment remains authoritative. U07 Run a several-second job and watch history, then wait after completion Elapsed advances every second while running, stops at completion; status, exit code and logs agree. U09 Configuration → Refresh; run bitloom --co

title: R01 — Incremental recipe and image builds
text: Set top target to busybox. Run Build target twice. Expected: successful jobs in history and less work on the second build. Run List recipe tasks, Dry run and Parse metadata. Progress represents task messages observed in logs, not CPU usage or an exact remaining-time estimate. Setscene and normal task phases may have different counters; a 100% observed counter alone does not mean the process exited. Run Fetch recipe sources, Unpack recipe, Apply recipe patches, Configure recipe, Compile recipe, Install recipe and Package recipe on busybox. Force compile should execute compilation even when otherwise current. Run custom task with target busybox and task listtasks and check the generated command. Set core-image-minimal: Build target and Build root filesystem. Verify completion by success/exit 0, then locate the image manifest and rootfs archive through Runtime directory at /work/build/tmp/deploy/images/qemux86-64.

title: R02 — Cleanup behavior
text: On the dedicated workspace, run Clean recipe work directory on busybox, then rebuild. Record work/sstate reuse. Run Clean recipe + sstate and rebuild; local recipe sstate is removed, while configured mirrors may still supply results. Run Clean recipe + sstate + downloads only when you deliberately want source removal and refetch; record the affected recipe and rebuild afterward. It does not mean delete every shared cache file.

title: R03 — Fetch and download audit
text: Run Fetch all target dependencies on core-image-minimal. Inspect downloads through Runtime directory, and run Download audit in Workbench for host-visible cache paths. Expected: fetch success and actual inventory/report. Host cache inventory cannot discover Docker-private files by guessing host paths; use runtime operations when that filesystem is not mounted on the host.

title: 5. Create a layer and recipes from the TUI
L01 — Layer creation and registration
text: F2 → Create layer, path /work/meta-bitloom. Expected: conf/layer.conf and generated skeleton. Inspect it with Analysis → Runtime file. Show layers and priorities does not list the new layer until registered. F2 → Add layer with the same path; Show layers and priorities should include it. Also test Show recipes, Show recipe appends, Show overlaid recipes and Show cross-layer dependencies. An empty report can be correct; record it rather than inventing conflicts. Remove layer, confirm it disappears, then add it again. Removal unregisters the layer; it does not delete its files. Generated bblayers.conf changes may be replaced by kas, so make registration reproducible in L03.

title: L02 — New recipe and file handling
text: Metadata → New file, or Analysis → Create runtime file. Enter: /work/meta-bitloom/recipes-example/bitloom-hello/bitloom-hello_1.0.bb Choose a recipe template, then replace its content with: SUMMARY = "Bitloom manual acceptance recipe" LICENSE = "CLOSED" S = "${WORKDIR}" do_install() { install -d ${D}${bindir} printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "Hello from Bitloom v1"\n' > ${D}${bindir}/bitloom-hello chmod 0755 ${D}${bindir}/bitloom-hello } CLOSED is only for this private test fixture. Use the actual license and checksums in distributable recipes. Expected: missing parent folders are created, the recipe is saved inside the selected runtime, and its containing directory opens in Analysis. Repeat creation at the same path: an error appears and existing content remains unchanged. Cancel another unsaved file: it must not exist. Also create a notes.txt using the empty template and verify its directory listing. Edit the saved recipe with Edit runtime file; change v1 to v2. Verify a backup is reported. Open an editor, change the same file externally before saving, then Save: the hash conflict must reject the stale edit. Creating/editing metadata while this session has a queued/running build is rejected.

title: L03 — Persist the layer and image customization in kas
text: On the HOST, create kas-testbook.yml at the checkout root using your IDE. Alternatively create it from New file with a host profile pointed at the checkout. A kas/container file dialog targets the container, so do not assume a host path is available there. header: version: 14 includes: - tests/integration/kas-minimal.yml repos: manual-experiment: path: /work/meta-bitloom local_conf_header: manual-experiment: | IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " bitloom-hello" Duplicate manual-kas in F4, call it manual-layer, keep the same KAS_WORK_DIR and container environment, and set kas_file to kas-testbook.yml. Run Build kas configuration. Expected: kas registers the layer and the image manifest contains bitloom-hello. Build bitloom-hello separately, edit its greeting and rebuild both recipe/image. Changes should be detected without cleaning every time.

title: L04 — .bbappend and external refresh
text: Use New file → Recipe append to create /work/meta-bitloom/recipes-core/busybox/busybox_%.bbappend: SUMMARY:append = " (manual experiment)" Show recipe appends should match it. Resolve busybox environment and verify SUMMARY. Run Explain sstate differences before/after a metadata change and inspect what actually changed; a SUMMARY-only change need not force compilation. With a HOST profile, select a locally indexed layer/recipe and create, edit, then delete a .bb file from your IDE. Within five seconds Metadata should reflect each change. Its selected file/layer expansion should survive changes when still present. Container-only metadata is viewed through runtime operations: open Runtime directory and add/remove a file through a second kas shell. Within fifteen seconds while idle the listing should refresh. Automatic scans pause with a modal open. F3 rescans local metadata; Analyze refreshes a runtime directory immediately.

title: D01 — Existing recipe development
text: On busybox: Workspace status → Modify recipe → Workspace status → Build workspace recipe. Inspect the source directory reported by devtool; use Devtool review on that directory for status, commit and diff evidence. Make a source change with the runtime editor or an available editor in Open kas shell. Devtool build and Build image with workspace recipes should use the workspace. Commit source changes in the devtool source repository before Finish recipe into layer, destination /work/meta-bitloom. Inspect the emitted .bbappend/patches, then rebuild. Reset workspace recipe removes workspace integration; inspect retained source files separately. Use Update recipe from source as an alternative export experiment and inspect its actual destination/output. Do not run finish/update blindly against upstream layers.

title: D02 — Create a source-based recipe
text: Using New file, create these files under /work/bitloom-source: CMakeLists.txt: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16) project(bitloom_dev C) add_executable(bitloom-dev main.c) install(TARGETS bitloom-dev DESTINATION bin) main.c: #include <stdio.h> int main(void) { puts("Bitloom devtool fixture"); return 0; } Add a LICENSE file containing your chosen actual license. Run Add source as recipe with target bitloom-dev and path /work/bitloom-source. Expected: devtool creates workspace metadata; Build workspace recipe succeeds. Inspect the generated recipe rather than assuming the automatic license/build-system detection is correct. Finish into your layer and inspect exported files. Also run Create recipe from URL/source with source /work/bitloom-source: inspect the generated recipe output; this action does not promise to save it at a destination filename.

title: D03 — Interactive terminal handoff
text: Open kas shell: run pwd and a read-only bitbake-layers show-layers, then exit. Expected: the terminal is handed off and the TUI returns. Open recipe development shell on busybox, then exit. Run Configure help on a compatible recipe and inspect the options. Menuconfig and QEMU are covered in optional tests below.

title: A01 — Logs and controlled failure
text: Through Custom command run python3 -c 'print("ERROR: manual diagnostic fixture"); raise SystemExit(7)'. Expected: failed job, exit 7, actual log content and notification. This is an intentional test failure, not a successful Yocto build. Retry with F6: the same argv/profile is used, even after changing the active profile. Select a build log, search error with different case, clear search, toggle Errors and Pause/Resume. Expected: matching context, paused display with continued capture, and accumulated output after resume. Export log and verify the local file. In Task logs, filter/select/read a real task log; Failed task log requires a actual BitBake failure with a reported task-log path. Temporarily add a failing do_install body to bitloom-hello, build it, inspect the task log/notification, then restore the recipe and rebuild. Review backups rather than editing them as recipes.

title: A02 — Workbench
text: Resolve busybox environment; filter PN, PV, WORKDIR, S, B and MACHINE. Load recorded output, save/resolve a second environment after a metadata change, then Env diff: changes should match the experiment. Resolve one BitBake variable with variable MACHINE. Generate graph for core-image-minimal, load Dependencies and inspect direct, reverse and transitive edges using Why this task? Missing edges are reported as missing evidence, not proof of no dependency. Build history diff requires buildhistory commits; inspect its Git diff after image package changes. Build report should describe selected log status/task/sstate/warnings. Timings requires available timestamps/buildstats evidence; missing timing data should be reported. Download audit requires accessible cache paths.

title: A03 — Runtime files, artifacts and package ownership
text: Runtime directory /work/build/tmp/deploy/images/qemux86-64 → choose an actual artifact path. Runtime file previews text manifests; binary files should be exported through Export runtime artifact, first field runtime path, second field a new LOCAL destination. Expected: SHA-256 verified export; existing destinations rejected. Text previews are limited to 2 MiB, binary export to 1 GiB, listings to 2,000 entries. Use Artifacts → Read file and Rootfs inventory for HOST-visible artifacts. For a container-only rootfs, export it first and inspect the local copy with a host profile. Tar inventory is read-only and does not extract symlinks into the filesystem. List built packages, List package files with target busybox, Find package owning a path with /bin/sh, and Find recipe for package with busybox. For Package provenance set top target core-image-minimal and first field /bin/sh. Expected: pkgdata owner, recipe and available inclusion chains; alternatives and package-manager decisions can limit the explanation.

title: A04 — Every Analysis report
text: Operation Inputs/fixture Expected result Search metadata Search a known local recipe text File/line matches; container-only files are not silently treated as host files. Compare manifests Two LOCAL exported manifests, before/after bitloom-hello inclusion Added/removed/version/architecture changes agree with files. Sstate efficiency Selected real build log or LOCAL log path Observed hit/miss statistics, with unavailable data distinguished. Warning groups A real log with repeated warnings Grouped counts, not invented warnings. Failure diagnosis Select controlled failed job Diagnosis from actual captured text; sensitive values redacted in exported bundles. Runtime directory / file / edit / create / export L02 and A03 Covered creation, limits, backup, conflicts, refresh and hash checks. Build preflight /work/build Permissions, disk/inodes and config presence; advisory thresholds labelled. Capture snapshot /work/build, before/after image change JSON saved locally; configs/revisions/manifests/artifacts and observed image identity where available. Note the saved paths. Compare snapshots First and second LOCAL snapshot JSON paths Differences reflect your recorded change. Reproducibility bundle /work/build Local JSON bundle with actual profile/config/revision evidence and redaction; add a synthetic API_TOKEN=testbook-not-a-secret to the profile and verify redaction. It does not promise reproducible binaries by itself. Why rebuilding? First field busybox Captures printdiff/signature co

title: S01 — Queue, history and reconnect
text: Submit two short jobs; expected serial execution, queued/running transitions, correct final status. Start a longer recipe task, Ctrl+Q, reopen with exactly the same --state. Expected: persistent service and build continue, history/logs reconnect. Clients attached to the same service share its serial queue. For the overlap test, start a separate service with a DIFFERENT --state directory but the same profile/build directory: exclusive build ownership should reject simultaneous execution rather than race BitBake. Compare F6 retry after changing profiles: original job profile must be retained. After jobs finish, from another terminal: bitloom --state .manual-testbook --service-status bitloom --state .manual-testbook --service-stop Expected: actual state and idle shutdown. Start/reconnect again. A stop request while work is active must not silently terminate it. Test --embedded with a separate state and short job: Ctrl+Q stops owned jobs, unlike the default persistent session. Demo also uses embedded behavior.

title: S02 — Interruption and recovery
text: On a disposable build, F5 → Let finish: job continues. Host or freshly managed direct-container profiles can expose Graceful stop: sends one SIGINT and waits, with no automatic escalation. kas wrappers and existing containers do not guarantee the client PID; Graceful stop is disabled there. Record this as expected runtime-specific behavior. Force + recovery must show observed active recipes and only offer recovery when shutdown is confirmed. Owned kas-container jobs record the exact container stop result before recovery. With native kas wrappers/external servers verify remaining work before manually cleaning; termination of the wrapper is not proof that BitBake stopped. Recovery uses recipe clean, not editing .bb files. An observed active recipe is not proof of corruption. Rebuild afterward and preserve interruption logs.

title: C01 — Inventory and reviewed prune
text: Create deliberately disposable HOST cache fixtures from the checkout: python - <<'PY' from pathlib import Path import os, time root = Path('.manual-testbook/cache-fixture').resolve() for sub, names in {'downloads': ['example.tar.gz', 'example.tar.gz.done', 'partial.part', 'orphan.done'], 'sstate': ['example.siginfo']}.items(): folder = root / sub folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) for name in names: path = folder / name if path.exists(): continue path.write_text('Disposable manual cache fixture; not reusable Yocto data\n') old = time.time() - 40 * 86400 os.utime(path, (old, old)) print(root) PY In F4 add a host profile using the checkout root and set downloads/sstate to those printed absolute folders. It is for inventory/prune tests, not Yocto builds. Choose age 30 days. The fixture files are synthetic and must be labelled as such in evidence. For a HOST-visible dedicated cache, configure the profile's downloads/sstate paths. In Caches select Downloads or Shared state, Scan, filter by filename and choose an age. Expected: real counts/sizes/mtime, concrete candidates, cancellation leaves files intact. Confirm only against disposable fixture files, then rescan and verify those exact files are gone. Paths/symlinks outside the selected root must not be deleted. Running/queued jobs and advisory cache leases must prevent unsafe conflicting operations. For kas container-private paths, use Runtime directory and Cache reference plan. The local prune UI does not magically mount

title: C02 — Signatures
text: Dump signatures and Explain sstate differences on busybox. Find actual .siginfo/.sigdata paths using runtime directories, then Read signature file and Compare signature files with two real files. Expected: parsed signature evidence; no change can legitimately produce no difference. Run Cache reference plan with /work/build/sstate-cache only if that is the actual cache location (resolve SSTATE_DIR first), and second /work/build/tmp/stamps if present. Unproven entries are not declared safe to delete.

title: 12. Record results and restore the experiment
text: Use one row per case in your own result file: Case PASS / FAIL / N/A Runtime and profile Evidence path Notes / missing prerequisite B01 TODO Record Git commit, Python/Textual versions, Docker/Podman and kas versions, image digest, Poky commit, MACHINE/DISTRO, cache/mirror configuration and modified YAML. Preserve selected job IDs, exported logs/reports/snapshots and screenshots. A successful command entry point alone is not proof that its intended artifact was created. After testing, finish or reset devtool work deliberately, remove experiment appends/recipes only after saving wanted work, switch back to the base kas profile, and rebuild. Removing a package from IMAGE_INSTALL and rebuilding should remove it from the image manifest. Stop the service only when idle. Keep the manual work directory until evidence is saved; do not delete .validation or a shared cache as cleanup for this book. Automated implementation checks are complementary: python -m pytest -q python tools/check_testbook.py python tools/build_docs.py

title: 13. Developer acceptance
text: All fourteen researched workflows are implemented in F10 Developer, across sixteen views. This chapter is a manual checklist; implementation does not imply you have already tested the feature. Record PASS/FAIL/N/A with evidence for each case. The Developer guide gives exact field meanings and limits; the research map retains sources. No hardware/SDK/security report is fabricated to fill a missing prerequisite.

title: Shared procedure
text: Use K02 or K04, keep the queue idle while inspecting, and record the selected profile. F10 opens Developer; Tab selects controls, arrows select rows, Enter/Open follows a runtime path. The first field changes meaning with the view; read its placeholder. Capture writes a timestamped private JSON export and fills the baseline input once. After a change/build, Inspect again and Compare; later Capture preserves the original baseline. Choose another JSON path to change it. Save the comparison export as evidence. Case View or control Required fixture Manual result P01 Variable history Parsed recipe plus matching append TODO P02 Recipe context + Runtime browser Real runtime layer TODO P03 Rebuild evidence Before/after signatures TODO P04 Failure investigation Controlled failed task TODO P05 New layer Writable new runtime destination TODO P06 IDE / SDK bridge Supported release/build system and SDK TODO or N/A with reason P07 Image regressions Two actual images with buildhistory/pkgdata TODO P08 Build performance Actual buildstats; cgroup-v2 if applicable TODO P09 Clone + Resolved kas / multiconfig Independent profile; optional multiconfig TODO P10 Downloads / offline Local source fixture and populated downloads TODO P11 CVE / SBOM review Actual supported JSON reports TODO or N/A with reason P12 Kernel fragments + Upgrade baseline Kernel .config/fragment; upgrade fixture TODO or N/A with reason P13 Board laboratory Dedicated real SSH/serial/labgrid equipment TODO or N/A with reason P1

title: P01 — Follow a variable to its source
text: Set the Developer recipe to your fixture (bitloom-hello after P05, or chapter 5's recipe). Select Variable history, first field SUMMARY, Inspect. Select assignment-origin rows: Enter opens the actual runtime file at its line. Capture. In a matching append add SUMMARY:append = " (experiment)", Inspect again and verify the final value and both origins. Query PACKAGECONFIG and OVERRIDES to inspect override context; an inactive override must not be presented as winning. Edit the origin externally while idle, wait for STALE (up to fifteen seconds), and verify Capture/Compare requires a fresh Inspect. Restore your append after recording evidence. Clear the recipe for a global variable; with configured multiconfig, repeat using mc:debug:RECIPE and verify that datastore identity is preserved.

title: P02 — Navigate real runtime files
text: Choose Recipe context for the fixture, Inspect, and inspect FILE/PV/appends/S/B/T/sysroots. Select S and Enter: Runtime browser opens the evaluated directory. Arrow/Enter through source files; open a file, save a greeting change with backup, then close and Inspect. Enter /work/meta-bitloom-dev in the browser's first field and .bb in its second field for a bounded recursive filename search. Create a file through Analysis/New file or chapter 5, refresh and verify it appears; delete your own test file externally, refresh and verify it disappears. Symlinks are labelled; edits through symlinks are refused. Repeat at 80×24 and 60×20: controls scroll, table/report remain reachable and return after resizing.

title: P03 — Investigate a rebuild
text: Build your fixture, choose Rebuild evidence and Run Dump signatures. When the queue finishes, Inspect and Capture. Edit its installed greeting/source, build again and dump signatures again. Inspect, open a signature row, and save actual diffsigs/printdiff evidence. Compare the capture. Potential dependency paths are labelled as evidence, not promised rebuild totals. Repeat without changing metadata: record the real result, which may reuse tasks and may still retain the last available historical signature pair. If paired sigdata is absent, record incomplete evidence rather than claiming no change or an invented cache-miss cause.

title: P04 — Connect the failed task, script and log
text: Use A01's deliberate bbfatal or create a matching append containing do_install:append() { bbfatal "Bitloom controlled task failure"; }. Force install and verify a genuinely failed history row. Select it in Builds, F10 → Failure investigation, leave the first field blank and Inspect. Open log.do_install and run.do_install rows; read the diagnostic context and Capture. Switch the active profile and inspect that selected old failure again: it must keep the original job/profile. Restore the append and rebuild successfully. The historical failure stays failed, and its captured evidence stays attached to that original job. Use an explicit runtime log path for a standalone investigation.

title: P05 — Create and register a licensed fixture from the TUI
text: F10 → New layer. Enter /work/meta-bitloom-dev, bitloom-hello, collection bitloomdev, your copyright owner, series scarthgap, new host YAML kas-bitloom-dev.yml, and CMake. Preview: check layer.conf, MIT text/checksum, main.c, CMakeLists.txt, recipe and kas registration. Cancel first and verify nothing was created. Repeat Preview → Create + register. A new derived profile selects the new overlay; original YAML/profile remain intact. F2 → Show configured layers, Show recipe appends and Build target bitloom-hello: successful parsing/build verifies registration. Build core-image-minimal and inspect its manifest for the package. Runtime browser → files/source/main.c → edit greeting → save → rebuild recipe/image. Existing destinations must be refused. Repeat with unique layer/name/YAML for Meson, Make, Python and Rust; inspect each complete source/license and build it on a release with the corresponding class/toolchain. SDK/compiler dependencies can make these real builds slow.

title: P06 — IDE source iteration
text: Choose IDE / SDK bridge for the CMake fixture, first field core-image-minimal, Inspect. Record S/B/compiler/sysroots/architecture and actual ide-sdk help. Configure F4 source_mappings only if the runtime source is truly host-visible. Run Export IDE mappings/database; inspect the export and mapped compile_commands.json if available, including -I/sysroot arguments. Generate IDE SDK queues release-native devtool ide-sdk after the probe. In the supported IDE/container context, change and build the greeting with the generated cross-toolchain; verify binary architecture and deployed image/debug symbols match. An unavailable IDE command, missing compile database or inaccessible Docker-private source is a prerequisite finding. Mark the interactive SDK/debug portion N/A until its requirements are supplied.

title: P07 — Compare images and trace a package
text: In an isolated kas overlay enable INHERIT += "buildhistory" and build the image. F10 → Image regressions, recipe core-image-minimal, Inspect → Capture. Record that package sizes identify their source (exact pkgdata bytes or normalized buildhistory KiB). Add your fixture with IMAGE_INSTALL, rebuild the same image/machine/distro/libc/multiconfig, Inspect → Compare. Expect an added package with recipe owner, installed file additions and byte deltas. Select that package → Trace selected package inclusion → Run. Change a fixture-installed file mode, rebuild and compare against a new deliberate baseline; record permission/owner/link differences from buildhistory. A different-machine/image baseline must be rejected. Missing buildhistory is unavailable, not an empty successful comparison.

title: P08 — Find measured bottlenecks
text: Enable buildstats in your test configuration, run a real build, then Build performance → Inspect with a blank first field for the latest session. Record slow tasks, timeline, measured task span and runtime cgroup/pressure/disk evidence. Capture, repeat a comparable build and Compare durations. Parallel durations must not be added to claim elapsed wall time. To test limits, configure a dedicated container with known cgroup-v2 CPU/memory limits and verify them separately from the host cards. Unavailable pressure/cgroup-v1 files or absent buildstats must be labelled. The probe measures its current runtime; it does not reconstruct old container usage.

title: P09 — Clone profiles and inspect multiconfig
text: F10 → Clone (also F4 → Clone). Choose a unique name and a separate absolute build directory, for example /tmp/bitloom-debug-work/build. For kas verify KAS_WORK_DIR still points to the original source workspace and KAS_BUILD_DIR is the new absolute directory; local layers remain available and the external build mount appears as /build. Select Resolved kas / multiconfig → Inspect → Capture; change a copied composition, re-inspect and Compare the real merged dump. Check the resolved machine/distro: profile hints do not rewrite a base YAML. Run Generate kas lock and inspect the release-native result. With actual BBMULTICONFIG configured, query mc:debug:RECIPE in Variable history and Recipe context and build the target through F2. Capture the context. Different profiles keep original job identity; one build directory cannot be owned by two cooperating builders, and the current service queue remains serial. Preserve the original profile/settings.

title: P10 — Diagnose downloads and verify offline readiness
text: Choose Downloads / offline, recipe your fixture, Inspect. Record mirror/cache/network variables and URI DNS observations. Induce a missing URI and separately a bad checksum in an isolated tiny source recipe (save its original metadata first); fetch and inspect the failed log through the first field or selected log. Expect distinct evidence categories; restore each change. Run Prepare source mirrors and wait for success; Run Verify fetch offline and separately Verify full build offline. Each job must record the actual result with BB_NO_NETWORK in its temporary BitBake configuration. A successful fetch check is not a claim that kas bootstrap or the full build needs no network. Restore the recipe and save original logs.

title: P11 — Review actual CVE/SPDX evidence
text: Run supported CVE/SPDX actions after Runtime capabilities identifies their tasks. Locate the real JSON report with Runtime browser. In CVE / SBOM review enter its absolute runtime path, Inspect → Capture. Record package/version/license, upstream issue status and available report/database dates. Build/import a second actual report and Compare for new/changed statuses. Select an issue → Record selected issue review → Run; enter owner/reason/future YYYY-MM-DD expiry. Inspect again: original status is retained and the separate review appears. Missing/unsupported reports must be unavailable; a review is not a patch or proof of non-exploitability. Expired saved reviews must be visibly labelled. Record N/A without suitable reports/configuration.

title: P12 — Check kernel fragments and recipe upgrades
text: For a kernel fixture, use Kernel fragments with recipe virtual/kernel, first field the fragment and second field final .config (or blank for evaluated B/.config). Inspect requested enabled/disabled values against actual values. Run Kernel config check, Export kernel diff and Menuconfig where actual listtasks supports them. Record mismatches and release tool results; no automatic fix is implied. Separately clone the profile, choose Upgrade baseline for a small recipe, Inspect → Capture before change; perform a controlled version/revision or devtool upgrade, parse/build, re-inspect and Compare. Versions may change while machine/distro/libc/multiconfig must remain compatible. Check active appends, patches, layer commits and dirty status; retain original kas pins and source edits. Mark unavailable kernel/upgrade operations N/A with prerequisites.

title: P13 — Use a real board and retain evidence
text: F10 → Devices; configure actual SSH/serial or labgrid equipment using the Developer guide schema. Board laboratory → Inspect; Enter selects a device. Run Device status and verify actual output; disconnect it and record the failed/unavailable result. Export the artifact to a local path (Analysis Export runtime artifact), put that path in the second field, and use a real devtool workspace recipe for Deploy recipe. Inspect the evidence JSON: hash/device/job/result are recorded; deploy transfers recipe outputs and must not claim that the referenced image was flashed. Run your explicit test_argv and verify its actual exit code/log. Console uses the real terminal and records transcript/exit status. For labgrid, verify show/acquire/release and use power cycle only on your dedicated place. N/A without actual equipment; there is no simulated board PASS.

title: P14 — Probe optional tasks and verify stopping
text: Runtime capabilities → Inspect your fixture and an image: record installed tools, task names, release and device/terminal prerequisites. In F2 choose an optional task absent from that probe; the recent result disables it with the missing task, or a fresh pre-submission probe refuses it before queueing. Refresh after configuration changes. Test missing ide-sdk/device tools similarly. On an expendable owned kas-container build, F5 → Let finish first; then in a separate run use Force + recovery. Record the unique Bitloom container name and Shutdown evidence observations: exact container stop result, client result and recovery eligibility. Confirm its container is gone/stopped using the same engine. Recipe recovery is offered only after confirmed termination; observed active tasks are at risk, not proof of corruption. Native kas wrappers/existing containers remain guarded when shutdown is unconfirmed. A new kas shell sees a separate namespace and must not be used as proof that an old server exited. Restart an old persistent service only after its queue is idle when installing the new version.

title: Developer evidence ledger
text: Save P01–P14 results with profile/release, inputs, baseline/current captures, comparison files and job IDs/logs. Optional N/A entries must name the missing hardware, task, report or SDK. Automated reproduction complements this book: python tools/validate_developer.py --build python tools/capture_developer.py python -m pytest -q python tools/check_testbook.py python tools/build_docs.py The validation helper's --image opt-in builds a full fresh image; its default --build validates a small recipe and offline/failure recovery paths. Read result.json rather than treating executable probe PASS as proof of missing image artifacts. Restore your experimental changes and keep the original state/history as described in chapter 12.

title: 14. Keyboard, web, compliance, Studio and teams
text: Run on the demo first (bitloom --demo), then on the real kas-scarthgap/kas-wrynose profiles from python tools/prepare_validation.py --release both where a case says so.

title: U01 — Keyboard-only session
text: Do not touch the mouse. Expected for each step: 1…0 open each section and focus its list; [/] cycle; the rail highlight follows. In Builds the footer and buttons show s r e p x i f c; e toggles errors only; typing /err puts the letters in the search field without toggling; Esc returns focus to History. 2 then j/k move in the metadata table; t (Recipes uses t for the tree) focuses the layer tree. 1, t, type a target (several separated by spaces), Enter: the build is queued at once, as with b and Build; a target such as a; id is refused and the field keeps focus. F2 opens the command center: ↓/↑ change the operation from the filter, Tab Tab reaches the inputs, Enter queues. P opens the profile switcher (j/k, Enter); ?, F1 and Ctrl+G open the keyboard reference; Ctrl+X closes it. Ctrl+P lists sections, Studio, console builds and every operation.

title: U02 — nano keys in editors
text: 9, l opens local.conf. ^K ^K cuts two lines, ^U pastes them back, ^W searches (Enter selects the match, Alt+W finds the next), ^X refuses once while the buffer is modified, ^O writes a timestamped .bak- backup, ^X closes. The same keys work in the profile editor (F4), runtime files and the new-file dialog; forms confirm with ^O.

title: W01 — Start the web dashboard securely
text: bitloom --web --no-browser --port 8765 --config .validation/profiles.json --state .validation curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/state # 401: token required curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'X-Bitloom-Token: wrong' http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/state # 401 Expected: the printed URL carries #token=…; opening it shows Connected and the service pid. The token disappears from the address bar after load. A TUI on the same --state shows the same history.

title: W02 — Follow, stop and retry from the browser
text: Queue a build with b (or Operations, q). Expected: a Build started toast; the progress bar is indeterminate, then striped with task N of M; output streams; the TUI shows the same job with a spinner. Open Summary/Sstate reuse/Warnings/Timings with u, o, w, m. Search with /, toggle errors with e. g (graceful) or s (force, confirm) stops it with a toast; r retries. A failure raises an error toast whose Open summary button jumps to the summary.

title: W03 — Palette, phone and light theme
text: Ctrl+K, type sbom: the palette lists the SBOM section and operations. Resize the browser below 900 px or open it on a phone: one column, scrolling navigation, toasts at the bottom. With the system light theme the page switches palettes; with reduce motion animations stop.

title: V01 — Release awareness
text: On demo-scarthgap (or kas-scarthgap): F2, type sbom, ↓ to Recipe CVE analysis from its SBOM. Expected: (not in this release), a disabled Queue button and “use Run recipe CVE check (cve-check) instead”. On demo-wrynose (or kas-wrynose) the same operation is offered and cve is refused the other way round. In the web dashboard the Operations dialog shows the same refusal. bitloom --ci sbom-cve-recipe:busybox --profile kas-scarthgap prints a skip warning and writes <skipped> in JUnit.

title: V02 — SBOM quality
text: 6, s (or bitloom --sbom). On demo-wrynose: SPDX 3.0.1, PURL 67%, supplier 67%, VEX affected 1 · fixed 1 · not affected 1, affected CVE-0000-0001. On demo-scarthgap: SPDX 2.2 with CPE coverage. On a real Scarthgap build: the image appears as …rootfs-<timestamp>.manifest (the SPDX 2.2 archive is read through the manifest and tmp/deploy/spdx), supplier 0% because of the OpenEmbedded placeholder, and CVEs recorded fixed by recipes.

title: V03 — SBOM settings
text: 9, s. Move with j/k; the right pane explains each option, its CRA relevance and release window. On Scarthgap, sbom-cve-check on image builds shows n/a and Space refuses it; Supplier, SPDX 2.2 accepts a name. Toggle Generate SPDX SBOMs and Build history, ^O. Expected: a managed block in build/conf/local.conf plus a .bak- backup (host/container), or bitloom-sbom.yml appended to the kas profile's kas_file. Reopen: the states persist. v queues bitbake-getvar for the selected variable.

title: V04 — CRA readiness
text: 9, c and bitloom --cra --config … --state …. Expected: the release support line, SBOM/identifier/licence/VEX/analysis/traceability/disposition/reproducibility checks, the 2026-09-11 and 2027-12-11 milestones and the EN 40000-1-3 note; --cra exits 2 when any check warns. The web SBOM & CRA section (5) shows the same checks with gauges.

title: N01 — Studio: your own distribution
text: 2, c. Expected: kinds on the left; Distribution selected. On the demo, the target layer is meta-demo; change the id to demo-os and watch the preview. ^O creates meta-demo/conf/distro/demo-os.conf; the profile's DISTRO becomes demo-os (top bar). Repeat: Studio refuses to overwrite. Try Image recipe on Wrynose: debug-tweaks is not offered; on Scarthgap it is.

title: N02 — Studio on a kas profile and in the browser
text: On kas-scarthgap, create a Product layer meta-acme, then an Image recipe in it. Expected: kas-studio-meta-acme.yml appended to kas_file with the layer as a repository and target: acme-image; b builds it after a kas build registers the layer. In the web Studio (6) the same forms preview live; Create files raises a toast with a Build button.

title: T01 — Headless CI matrix
text: bitloom --config .validation/profiles.json --state .ci --ci kas-build --profile kas-scarthgap \ --junit results.xml --summary summary.json --annotations github Expected: ::group:: sections around the build output, error/warning annotations, results.xml with one test case per job, summary.json with status, sstate hit rate, warnings, failed tasks and new images; exit code 0 on success. Ctrl+C stops the running job cleanly (exit 130).

title: T02 — Team profiles
text: Create /tmp/team.json with {"profiles": [{"name": "team-demo", "root": "<demo root>"}]} and add "include": ["/tmp/team.json", "/tmp/missing.json"] to your profiles file. Expected: P lists team-demo marked team; F4 shows only your own profiles plus the include list; Configuration warns about /tmp/missing.json; saving profiles keeps the include.

title: T03 — Setup, filesystem and network checks
text: 9 and bitloom --doctor (--network to probe). Expected: host rows (cores, memory, Python, locale, inotify, open files, engines, WSL hint), filesystem rows for the build directory, TMPDIR, DL_DIR and SSTATE_DIR, and n probing configured mirrors/hash equivalence/PR servers without downloading.

title: T04 — Images, fleet and console builds
text: 6, m lists every image per MACHINE with sizes and package counts. Developer → Board view → Fleet status (or bitloom --fleet) probes all configured devices at once and writes fleet-status.json. Run a build directly in a kas shell, outside Bitloom; then 1, c: the console build appears classified, Enter opens it with search and errors-only, and the web dashboard lists it under Console builds.

title: T05 — Project launcher script
text: Create a script that accepts kas subcommands and shell -c CMD, for example: cat > /tmp/launcher.sh <<'SH' #!/bin/bash # Configuration chosen by $YML; kas subcommand as arguments. if [ "$1" = "shell" ] && [ "$2" = "-c" ]; then exec kas-container shell "$YML" -c "$3"; fi exec kas-container "$@" "$YML" SH chmod +x /tmp/launcher.sh Add a profile with "mode": "wrapper", "launcher": ["/tmp/launcher.sh"], "environment": {"YML": "tests/integration/kas-minimal.yml", "KAS_WORK_DIR": "<work dir>"}. Expected: Configuration shows the launcher as OK; Build kas configuration runs /tmp/launcher.sh build; Resolve recipe environment runs /tmp/launcher.sh shell -c 'bitbake -e …'.

title: J01 — Guided setup of an existing project
text: Create a folder with a kas file and a launcher script (the T05 script works), or use one of your projects. Configuration → w → o, type the folder, Enter. Expected: proposals with evidence (launcher script reading $YML, kas file with MACHINE, Poky checkout if present); ↑/↓ fills the form; checks show ✔/▲/✖ live and block saving on ✖ (for example an empty KAS_WORK_DIR for kas-container); ^O makes the profile active and the top bar, Recipes and Configuration reload. Opening the same folder again switches to its profile. Start Bitloom in an empty directory with a new --config: the guided setup opens by itself. Repeat in the web dashboard (8 → Set up a project).

title: J02 — New project
text: w → n. Choose Wrynose, qemuarm64, core-image-base, product layer on. Expected: the preview shows kas.yml with bitbake/openembedded-core/meta-yocto pinned to yocto-6.0.2 and meta-<name>; ^O creates the folder with README, .gitignore, .git and the layer; the profile is active; b starts the first kas build. A non-empty folder or an invalid name is refused. In the web dashboard: 8 → New project, live preview, Create project, toast with Build it.

title: J03 — Clone from Git
text: w → g, enter an HTTPS or SSH URL of a project (or file:///path/to/repo). Expected: the destination is suggested until you edit it; ^O starts a Clone job visible in Builds; on success the guided setup opens on the clone. An existing destination or an option-like URL is refused. Web: Clone from Git, then the Set it up toast.

title: V05 — Vulnerabilities
text: On demo-wrynose: 6, v. Expected: 3 unpatched findings ordered critical (CVE-0000-0002, 9.8), high, medium; /openssh filters; the detail shows source, detail and summary; r opens the review dialog and, after saving, the Review column shows owner and expiry; x opens the export menu: each format (Markdown, HTML, CSV, JSON, SARIF) writes <state>/exports/vulnerabilities-<profile>-<time>.<ext> with the findings shown; the Markdown and HTML reports link every CVE to NVD, CVE.org and OSV and end with the Yocto remediation steps; g scans the newest SPDX SBOM with Grype when installed (otherwise it explains). bitloom --vulns --min-cvss 9 --fail-on-unpatched exits 2; with --min-cvss 9.9 it exits 0. On a real Wrynose build with the sbom-cve-check fragment enabled, the report from tmp/deploy/images appears as source. bitloom --vulns --format md -o report.md (also html, csv, json, sarif, --all-statuses) writes the same reports. Web: 5 → Vulnerabilities with chips, filters and the Export menu (download in the chosen format); CRA readiness shows Unpatched vulnerabilities.

title: H01 — Build notifications
text: 9, o: tick failed and success, set the minimum to 0, keep desktop on and enter an ntfy topic (https://ntfy.sh/<random-topic>, subscribed on your phone) as webhook; ^T. Expected: a desktop notification (on WSL a Windows notification), the terminal bell and a push on the phone. Run a short failing command (F2 → custom python3 -c 'exit(1)'), close the TUI before it ends in persistent mode: the notification still arrives (sent by the service). Set the minimum to 600: short jobs stay quiet. In the web dashboard enable the bell button, switch to another tab and let a build end: a browser notification appears.

title: H02 — ETA, comparison and tmp/work
text: Run the same build twice. Expected: during the second run the Tasks card and the web progress line show ETA ~… with its basis (task rate, previous runs); after it, 1, d (web: Compare tab) compares durations, executed vs setscene tasks, sstate hit rate and warnings. 5, w (or bitloom --work-usage) lists the largest recipe work directories, says whether rm_work is enabled and suggests clean commands.

title: B04 — GitHub release workflow
text: In GitHub → Actions → Release Bitloom → Run workflow, enter a new version (for example 0.2.0) and optionally tick draft or prerelease. Expected: tests pass, the job builds bitloom-<version>.tar.gz, the wheel, bitloom_<version>_all.deb and SHA256SUMS, installs the .deb and smoke-tests it, attaches the assets to the workflow run and creates the v<version> release. An existing tag is refused. Locally, python tools/build_release.py 0.2.0 --output /tmp/release produces the same files.

title: E01 — Damaged files and odd inputs
text: Run each step in a scratch copy (cp -r .bitloom /tmp/bl, then --config /tmp/bl/profiles.json --state /tmp/bl). Expected: a one-line message naming the file, never a Python traceback. Write {nope into profiles.json and run bitloom --cra: exit 2, …profiles.json is not valid JSON. An empty profiles.json behaves like a first start; a file without "active" uses its first profile; "active": "ghost" lists the defined profiles. Write not a database into history.sqlite3 and run bitloom --ci parse: exit 2, history.sqlite3 cannot be used … move it away. Write [1, 2] into security-reviews.json: CRA readiness shows Vulnerability dispositions as WARN with the reason, Vulnerabilities lists it, and recording a review (r) is refused without changing the file. Put a truncated *.spdx.json and a *.sbom-cve-check.yocto.json containing {"package": "nope"} next to the image: --sbom and --vulns report each file's problem and keep analysing the others. Build target core-image-minimal busybox queues one BitBake command with both targets; a; id, $(id) or a task compile; id are refused with Not a BitBake target / Not a task name, in the TUI, in the web dashboard and in --ci build:…. Web API: POST /api/jobs with "values": "x" answers 400 with a JSON error; DELETE /api/state answers 405.

title: D01 — Documentation site
text: python tools/serve_docs.py --port 8000, open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Expected: the landing page with feature filter, runtime tabs and screenshot lightbox. Open the User guide: a sidebar lists every page (the current one highlighted), On this page follows the scroll, each page ends with Previous / Next. Press / (or Ctrl+K), type sbom-cve-check: results from several pages with highlighted terms; ↓ and Enter open the section. The ☾/☀ button switches theme and is remembered after a reload; without a choice the site follows the system theme. Code blocks show Copy on hover. At phone width, ☰ opens the page list and nothing scrolls sideways.

title: Research and implementation map
text: Research and implementation map Research reviewed on 2026-10-10. All fourteen workflows below now have implemented controls in F10 Developer. See the Developer guide for inputs/operations and chapter 13 of the manual testbook for concrete acceptance cases. Implementation status and validation coverage are separate: hardware, complete SDK debugging and release-specific reports still require their real prerequisites.

title: What developers are struggling with
text: Public discussions describe opaque configuration, confusing errors and lengthy feedback loops. A developer learning Yocto describes difficulty understanding variables and locating the actual failure in an August 2026 discussion. Another describes spending working days chasing configuration changes across projects in an August 2023 discussion. A March 2025 beginner discussion highlights friction between an intended image change and the resulting system. These are individual experiences, not a representative developer survey. They identify problems worth investigating; they do not establish demand percentages or prove which feature is most popular. The priorities below are Bitloom's assessment of daily value, considering what the application already provides. Technical foundations are checked against upstream documentation, rather than community advice alone.

title: Answering the criticisms of earlier Yocto interfaces
text: Research reviewed on 2026-10-12. Earlier graphical front ends were criticised and some were retired; Bitloom is designed around those lessons. The left column records documented problems, the right column how Bitloom responds. It is a design rationale, not a claim that Bitloom replaces these tools. Documented problem Bitloom's response Hob was tightly woven into BitBake internals, fragile, needed constant QA, was tied to GTK+ 2 and was removed in 2016 (removal discussion). Uses only public command-line interfaces and their output (bitbake, bitbake-layers, devtool, kas, bitbake-getvar, logs and deploy files); no imports of BitBake internals. A terminal UI plus a standard-library web page, nothing to keep in sync with a GUI toolkit. Toaster must be running before a build to record it, needs its own Django setup and database, struggles with non-Poky layouts, and the project lists it among components with little maintainer time (Toaster manual, 2025 status reports). Reads evidence after the fact: console builds from tmp/log/cooker (builds started anywhere), task logs, deploy directories, SPDX documents and buildstats. One pip/.deb install, SQLite history only for its own queue, kas and split-repository (Wrynose) layouts, containers and project launcher scripts. knotty output floods beginners; finding the failing task and its cause is hard, and messages labelled ERROR are not always the root cause (user report, BitBake discussion). Errors-only filter with context, failed task logs

title: Implemented workflow map
text: Case Implemented interaction Evidence and practical boundary P01 Variable history with origin Enter-to-edit Actual getvar/evaluated datastore, OVERRIDES, file/line history and stale fingerprints; global/recipe/multiconfig identity remains explicit. P02 Recipe context and selectable Runtime browser Evaluated provider/appends/source/build/temp/sysroot paths plus bounded recursive filename search; logs/scripts remain read-only. P03 Rebuild evidence Paired sigdata/diffsigs, printdiff and potential reverse task dependencies; missing pairs/cache proof is incomplete evidence, not a guessed causal count. P04 Failure investigation Original job/profile, reported task log/script and diagnostic context; relative source locations are not guessed. P05 New layer preview and registration Complete MIT-licensed CMake/Meson/Make/Python/Rust fixtures, checksum, source and layer.conf; new kas overlay/profile or queued add-layer. Existing destinations refused; parse/build establishes successful registration. P06 IDE / SDK bridge Actual ide-sdk probe/queue, source/sysroot/compiler identity and explicit mapping/compile-database exports; SDK generation/debugging depends on installed release, build system and accessible sources. P07 Image regressions and provenance Actual buildhistory/pkgdata packages, normalized byte sizes, file metadata and baseline deltas; reject incompatible contexts, expose missing reports. P08 Build performance Measured buildstats timeline/trends plus cgroup-v2/pressure/disk evi

title: Upstream foundations
text: Variable assignment histories, recipe/task datastores, task logs and signature differences use the installed release's tools described in Yocto debugging documentation. Runtime file/line navigation and connected captures are Bitloom's interface design. The Technical FAQ explains checks such as selected recipe versions when changes appear ineffective. The IDE bridge follows release-supported devtool ide-sdk behavior in the Scarthgap SDK manual. It probes the installed command before submitting; it does not promise every IDE/language or a host-visible Docker-private source tree. Image comparisons consume the package/file metadata described in buildhistory documentation. Performance uses buildstats and reports observable limits alongside measurements discussed in build-speed guidance. There is no automatic tuning or invented time-saved forecast. Profile isolation and configuration-specific targets are grounded in BitBake multiconfig documentation; profile cloning and a multiconfig datastore remain separate concepts. Fetch classification, mirrors and network-disabled checks use BitBake fetching behavior. Source readiness and complete build readiness have separate recorded outcomes. Security review retains original findings and separate local dispositions. Scarthgap vulnerability guidance describes mapping limitations; current security documentation describes newer SBOM-based workflows. title: Validation and remaining experiments
text: The validation report separates the earlier verified 4,064-task minimal-image build from new Developer probes and small-recipe/offline/controlled-failure validation. Parser fixtures verify deltas, cgroup/buildstats handling, CVE reviews and kernel fragment comparisons; UI tests verify runtime editing, preview/cancel, captures/staleness and compact layout. Executable probes can pass while an optional artifact remains unavailable. Run P01–P14 in the testbook and keep actual captures/logs. Device deployment/console, complete interactive IDE cross-build/debugging, new CVE database scans, full kernel compilation and an end-to-end Podman build need the corresponding environment. The implemented controls expose these prerequisites rather than marking them successful. This research map records shipped behavior; it is not a delivery-date or community-demand survey.
